title: Define core-owned, rules-pack-bound canonical character sheet authority
description:
TWO FIXED CONSTRAINTS (not questions to revisit):
1. CORE-OWNED: the authoritative character sheet lives behind a core-owned model and persistence/API boundary in @eshyra/core, NOT in CLI-only JSON files. CLI, future web, and future app UXes all call the same core character-sheet APIs (repo principle: UI-agnostic core, thin CLI).
2. RULES-PACK-BOUND: a character sheet is valid only for the rules system, rules pack, and schema version that produced it. It is NOT generic 'D&D-ish' data and is NOT a cross-pack universal model. The sheet stays pinned to the pack it was created under; a rules-pack upgrade must never silently rewrite a character.

This is already where FinalizedCharacter points: it carries schemaVersion, system ('dnd5e-srd'), rulesPackId (which encodes pack version, e.g. rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1), recipeId, creationMode, plus frozen class/ancestry/background refs and rules-derived fields. That type should become (or convert into) the core-owned, pack-bound canonical sheet.

Current state:
- Core live SQLite 'character' rows are sparse — fine for prompt context, not a long-term authority.
- FinalizedCharacter is a rich core TYPE but its PERSISTENCE is CLI-side (createFileFinalizedCharacterStore writes JSON).
- Leveling needs one authoritative, pack-bound record for class refs, provenance, progression events, proficiencies, equipment, languages, spells, HP, ability scores, derived values.

Non-goals:
- Do NOT design a universal character schema making 5e / Pathfinder / future systems mutually interchangeable.
- Do NOT support in-place rules-pack migration as part of leveling.
- Do NOT assume a character is playable under a different rules pack without an explicit conversion.

Open sub-decisions (the real remaining work; storage shape only):
- Versioned JSON document first, normalized tables later, or both via projection (recommended lean: core-owned versioned document + sparse live-state projection).
- Whether FinalizedCharacter evolves into the canonical pack-bound sheet type or is converted into one after creation.
- How the sparse live 'character' table relates to it (projection/cache/prompt summary — NOT an independent authority).
- Migration path from existing CLI finalized-character JSON files into core-owned storage.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical sheet records include characterId, schemaVersion, rulesSystem/system, rulesPackId (with pack version), and enough provenance to validate future reads/writes.
- Persistence and read/write APIs for the canonical sheet are owned by core; CLI calls them now, web/app later.
- Core progression APIs REFUSE to apply progression when the acting rules pack does not match the sheet's rulesPackId/rulesSystem (fail closed on mismatch).
- It is defined whether FinalizedCharacter evolves into the canonical pack-bound sheet type or is converted into one.
- The sparse live 'character' table's relationship to the canonical sheet is defined (projection/cache/prompt summary, not an independent authority).
- A migration path from CLI-side finalized-character JSON files into core-owned storage is defined.
- It is recorded that CLI-owned JSON persistence is no longer authoritative, and that cross-pack character conversion is a FUTURE explicit operation that creates a new character/sheet from old character information (new-character generation with imported source facts), NOT an in-place mutation or normal progression.
- Progression ledger (.2) and level-up engine (.8) are blocked on this boundary.
notes: PR #325 (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/325) — ADR 0011. Decision deliverable; implementation tracked as eshyra-lupf.14. Open for review; close on merge.
